tasks.short: Coordinate itinerary changes with ATC agencies.

steps.what: Retrieve and verify actual flight itinerary, proposed change and responsible ATC agency
inputs: actual current flight plan and itinerary version
actual requested change and responsible agency directory
outputs: checked itinerary-change context and actual ATC contact

steps.what: Coordinate changes to actual flight itineraries with appropriate ATC agencies
inputs: checked itinerary-change context and actual ATC contact
outputs: actual coordinated itinerary change and unresolved constraints

steps.what: Record and check exact final coordinated itinerary change, flight identity and agency destination
inputs: actual coordinated itinerary change and unresolved constraints
checked itinerary-change context and actual ATC contact
outputs: checked final actual itinerary change and exact permitted destination

steps.what: Commit the exact checked final itinerary-change record
inputs: checked final actual itinerary change and exact permitted destination

steps.what: Transmit the exact checked itinerary change through the actual authorised operational channel
inputs: checked final actual itinerary change and exact permitted destination

tasks.design: Configure native current-flight, change-source and agency-contact links in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}. The specialist verifies context, retains actual ATC coordination and exact change capture/check, then separately commits and transmits any required final operational message.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change coordination can repeat current-plan and agency-contact navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native flight/version/contact links can reduce retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Operational feasibility and actual agency agreement require coordination.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises a change that has not actually been agreed or is tied to the wrong flight.
tasks.altitude: Less change-context navigation; ATC coordination stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native flight/version/contact links can reduce context retrieval; they do not authorise itinerary changes or confer ATC clearance authority.

assumptions: Actual flight-plan owner supplies flight identity, current itinerary version and requested change; actual agency owner supplies contact/responsibility. Specialist verifies these in s1. Missing/stale data remains manual.
Actual coordination, agency responses, final change capture and complete checking remain retained. No autonomous rerouting, acceptance inference or clearance is assumed.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native links first; existing linked access earns zero saving. Commit/transmit each retain one percent and use the existing final content/authority check after the exact change exists.

Actual operational channel and delegated authority must permit the transmission. If coordination is entirely oral with no separate record/message, remove those branches and reweight actual work; do not invent duplicate dispatch or new approval ceremony.
research_questions: Can native links shorten preparation while preserving exact change and authority checks?

incremental.description: Maintain actual flight/version and agency contact links.

approvals.approved_version: s3 checked final actual itinerary change and exact flight/version destination; edits require recheck
s3 checked final actual itinerary-change message and exact authorised ATC destination/channel; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.50 context navigation = 10; minus 0.5 upkeep = 9.5. Half eligible gives 5 minus 0.5 = 4.5. Coordination, final capture/check, commit and transmission retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

inputs: actual checked plan issues and verification questions
outputs: actual plan verification findings and unresolved discrepancies

steps.what: Record and check final plan verification findings and any required civilian-agency message
inputs: actual plan verification findings and unresolved discrepancies
actual permitted disclosure scope and agency destination

tasks.design: Configure native current-plan and civilian-agency source links in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}. The specialist retains plan checks, agency verification and finding capture, then separately commits any actual record and transmits only the exact permitted final message.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plan checks can repeat source/version and civilian-agency navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source links can reduce retrieval without deciding plan acceptability.
tasks.still_hard: Actual discrepancies and disclosure permissions require operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist identifies an unresolved agency condition rather than assuming plan acceptance.
tasks.altitude: Less plan-source navigation; verification stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native plan/version/source links can support military-civilian coordination retrieval; they do not determine plan acceptance or permit disclosing restricted information.

assumptions: Actual military plan owner supplies version, identifiers, routing/timing and actual disclosure scope; actual civilian agencies supply current records/responses. Specialist verifies sources in s1 and retains all plan checking and discussion.
Only retrieval navigation loses time. No automatic plan clearance, inferred civilian acceptance or unrestricted data transfer is assumed. Actual findings are recorded after real agency checking.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native links first; existing source access earns zero saving. Record/message branches apply only when actually required; oral-only cases remove them and reweight actual work.

Routine commit/transmit each retain one percent and consume the existing final check after exact content exists. Actual authority and disclosure restrictions must hold; any other required final-owner approval remains actual work with no avoided time claimed.
research_questions: Can native links reduce retrieval while preserving complete plan and disclosure checks?
